scenario: [LDET.3.6.2]: `Float` comparison is IEEE 754's, and a NaN is unordered with everything, itself included -- `==`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` are false and `!=` is true. The NaN is `t.z / t.z` on a Float slot holding 0.0, so nothing folds and the division is IEEE (a Float operand, [LEXP.7.15.1]). One rule per operator; only the two `!=` rules may fire, in source order. A runtime that reads an unordered pair as equal fires `nan_eq_nan`, `nan_le_one` and `nan_ge_one` and not `nan_ne_nan`, as a `val_cmp` of `(a > b) - (a < b)` does. PATH PINNED: libds rete/eval.c's comparison arm through val_cmp / dbl_cmp; Mercury ds.eval's Float comparison.
rules_ds:
schema T scope logical:
    entity_id: String key
    z: Float mutable
    one: Float mutable

rule nan_ne_nan:
    T t where (t.z / t.z) != (t.z / t.z)
->
    log info "a"

rule nan_eq_nan:
    T t where (t.z / t.z) == (t.z / t.z)
->
    log info "b"

rule nan_lt_one:
    T t where (t.z / t.z) < t.one
->
    log info "c"

rule nan_le_one:
    T t where (t.z / t.z) <= t.one
->
    log info "d"

rule nan_gt_one:
    T t where (t.z / t.z) > t.one
->
    log info "e"

rule nan_ge_one:
    T t where (t.z / t.z) >= t.one
->
    log info "f"

rule nan_ne_one:
    T t where (t.z / t.z) != t.one
->
    log info "g"
